diagram_kind: staged iterated point blowups with strict-transform incidence changes
why_warranted: A schematic stage diagram can clarify that the construction first regularizes all components, then lowers the finite maximum of pairwise intersection multiplicities, and finally separates multiplicity-one contacts. Its useful content is the change in incidence among the named strict transforms across successive ambient blowups.

objects: pairwise distinct integral one-dimensional closed subschemes Y_1,...,Y_r with finite normalization
current closed point centers p_j in X_{j-1}
exceptional divisors over the chosen centers
strict transforms Y_i^(j) embedded in X_j
maps_and_relations: For each blowup center p_j, draw pi_j:X_j=Bl_{p_j}(X_{j-1})→X_{j-1}; the composite X_m→...→X_1→X_0 is the finite sequence in the theorem.
Show each current strict transform Y_i^(j) as a subscheme of X_j; centers may belong to more than one current curve.
Separate the initial regularization stage, where every component becomes a regular integral curve, from later contact-reduction stages.

At a maximum-multiplicity center for a pair, indicate that any remaining pairwise intersection over that center has strictly smaller multiplicity; at multiplicity one, indicate the pair's transforms become disjoint over the center.
In the terminal stage, show Y_i^(m)∩Y_j^(m)=∅ for i≠j and label each final transform regular.
scope_and_visual_conventions: Centers p_j are points on the current ambient scheme X_{j-1}; do not label all later centers as points of the original X_0.
The exceptional divisor can meet the strict transforms; the conclusion is pairwise disjointness among the Y_i^(m), not disjointness from exceptional divisors.
Do not depict a specific smooth surface or assume a two-dimensional ambient scheme: the theorem assumes a Noetherian scheme X.
A common center can lie on multiple components; the drawing should not impose a fixed number or pairwise simple-crossing geometry.
Keep intersection-multiplicity labels schematic and only use the stated properties: strict decrease at maximum centers and separation when multiplicity is one.

correctness_checks.ambient_map_directions_and_composition: pass: each blowup map is pi_j:X_j→X_{j-1}; their composite has source final ambient scheme and target original X_0
correctness_checks.strict_transform_ambient_indexing: pass: Y_i^(j) lies in X_j after the jth blowup; the center p_j is in X_{j-1}
correctness_checks.center_may_meet_multiple_components: pass: assignment explicitly allows centers on multiple components; the proof processes updated strict transforms
correctness_checks.regularization_hypotheses_and_preservati: pass: finite normalization is retained under the stated operations, and already regular curves remain regular by F2
correctness_checks.multiplicity_and_terminal_incidence: pass: step 3.1 strictly lowers remaining pairwise multiplicities from a maximum n≥2; step 3.2 separates multiplicity-one contacts; finite intersections and finite maxima are supplied by step 2.1
correctness_checks.terminal_scope: pass: only the final named strict transforms are pairwise disjoint regular curves; no claim is made that they avoid exceptional divisors
